items.title: You are paralysed multiple times every night
items.claim: During REM sleep, when most dreams occur, motor neurons to your skeletal muscles are actively inhibited. You cannot move. This is REM atonia — and when it fails, people act out their dreams.
items.prompt: Why does the brain paralyse you while dreaming?

options.text: To prevent acting out dream content — the same brain regions that command movement are active in REM as in waking, but spinal motor neurons are blocked from receiving the signals
To stop heart rate from rising

items.reveal_title: REM behavior disorder and Schenck's discovery
items.reveal:
The brainstem (specifically the pons and medulla) sends inhibitory signals to spinal motor neurons during REM. The motor cortex fires in patterns resembling waking; the descending commands reach the spinal cord but cannot trigger muscle contraction.

In REM Behavior Disorder (Schenck 1986), this paralysis fails. Patients punch, kick, vocalise and act out vivid dreams. RBD is strongly associated with later Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia — the brainstem regions controlling REM atonia degrade early in these conditions.

Narcolepsy with cataplexy is the opposite failure: REM-style atonia intrudes into waking life, triggered by emotion. Modafinil and other treatments stabilise the boundary between sleep states.
items.why: Sleep is imagined as 'off'. REM sleep is intensely active — and the body needs active suppression to prevent the brain's instructions reaching the muscles.

items.title: Lions get only 0.001% of the sun's energy that hit their grass
items.claim: Each trophic level passes about 10% of its energy to the next. Sun -> grass -> antelope -> lion. Three steps means lions retain 0.1% of grass energy. Add another step and you're down to 0.01%. The tenth-of-energy rule explains why food chains are short.

options.text: Most of the consumed energy goes to respiration (powering the consumer's metabolism), heat loss, and undigested waste; only a small fraction is converted into new tissue available to the next predator

items.reveal:
Raymond Lindeman (1942) measured energy flow in Cedar Bog Lake, Minnesota. He found progressive losses at each trophic level — formalising 'trophic efficiency'.

Typical values: primary producers fix ~1-2% of incident solar energy as net primary productivity. Herbivores extract ~10% of plant productivity. Carnivores ~10% of herbivore productivity. Top predators get a tiny fraction of the original solar input.

Consequences: food chains rarely exceed 4-5 trophic levels; predators have huge home ranges and small populations; ecosystems with apex predators are inherently fragile to disruption at the base.

The '10% rule' is an approximation. Efficiencies actually vary: ectotherms (fish, reptiles) can transfer 30-40% because they don't spend energy maintaining body heat. Endotherms (mammals, birds) burn most of what they eat to stay warm.

Vegetarian arguments often invoke this: feeding plants directly to people is ~10x more energy-efficient than routing them through livestock first.
items.why: Food chains feel boundless. Thermodynamics caps them at 4 or 5 links. Each predator carries the entropic cost of every prey it ate.

items.title: Light makes the inside of a chloroplast 1000 times more acidic
items.claim: In dark chloroplasts, stroma and thylakoid lumen are both about pH 7. Turn on the light: protons are pumped from stroma INTO thylakoid lumen. Lumen pH drops to ~5; stroma rises to ~8. That's a thousand-fold proton concentration difference.

options.text: The proton gradient drives ATP synthase: protons flow back through the enzyme from lumen to stroma, powering ATP synthesis. The light reactions store light energy as a transmembrane proton gradient, just as respiration does

items.reveal:
Light reactions in chloroplast thylakoid membranes:
1. Photosystem II uses light to oxidise water (releasing O2) and reduce plastoquinone. Protons are released INSIDE the lumen.
2. Cytochrome b6f passes electrons on while also pumping protons FROM stroma TO lumen.
3. Photosystem I uses light to push electrons to NADP+, making NADPH (in the stroma).
4. Net result: lumen accumulates protons, stroma loses them. pH gradient ~3 units (1000x concentration).

ATP synthase (CF1-CF0) in the thylakoid membrane lets protons flow back from lumen to stroma. The enzyme rotates, synthesises ATP from ADP and Pi. ATP and NADPH are released INTO the stroma, where the Calvin cycle uses them to fix CO2.

This is exactly analogous to mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. Same chemistry, opposite source — solar input rather than food oxidation. Both use the proton motive force to make ATP.

The parallel was predicted by Peter Mitchell in 1961 and confirmed experimentally over the next two decades.
items.why: Photosynthesis is taught as if it makes sugar directly from light. Light first powers a proton pump; the pump powers ATP synthesis; ATP plus NADPH then power sugar synthesis. Energy storage is layered.
